gate1.note: Motorcycles via independent dealers plus a captive lender; units x ASP with segment margins disclosed separately.

gate2.note: Brand-driven premium pricing, ~50% US heavyweight share, mid-30s gross margin, high-teens operating margin; US retail near cycle highs (FY2014, 2015-01-27).
First annual US retail decline: FY2015 -1.7% (2016-01-28), FY2016 -3.9% (2017-01-31). Aging core buyer, weak new-rider entry.
Pricing power visibly fails: FY2017 US retail -8.5% (2018-01-30), FY2018 -10.2%. The 2018-06-25 8-K states the ~$2,200/bike EU tariff would NOT be passed to customers.

gate3.note: DOJ/EPA Clean Air Act settlement (2016-08-18): ~340,000 'super tuner' defeat devices sold since 2008; $12M penalty + $3M mitigation. HOG denied liability, no admission.

gate1.note: Hardware, software, services plus Global Financing; segment disclosure adequate though Global Financing adds some leverage opacity.

gate2.note: Mainframe switching costs, software gross margin near 89%, pretax margin ~20%, revenue ~$106.9B (2011).

YoY revenue declines began Q2 2012 (2012-07-18) and reached four straight by Q1 2013 (2013-04-18, -5%); the streak ran 22 consecutive quarters to Q3 2017. Four straight known at the 2013 anchor, 8 at 2014, 12 at 2015, 16 at 2016, 20 at 2017.

Roadmap 2015 EPS target abandoned 2014-10-20; same day IBM agreed to PAY GlobalFoundries ~$1.5B to take the chip unit plus a $4.7B charge. FY2015 revenue $81.7B vs $99.8B in 2013; public cloud ceded to AWS/Azure.

gate3.note: SEC FCPA settlement (2011-03-18) $10M: cash to South Korean officials 1998-2003 and slush funds at Chinese travel agencies. Books-and-records/internal-controls charges, settled without admission.
SEC investigating how IBM reported cloud revenue; disclosed in a 2013 10-Q. SEC took no action (public 2014-06-03), and IBM changed its cloud disclosure.
New SEC investigation into revenue recognition (US, UK, Ireland) disclosed 2015-10-27.
ProPublica (2018-03-22) alleged systematic age-based targeting in US layoffs. Allegation only, no adjudication in the window.

gate1.note: Olefins/polyolefins, intermediates, refining: volume x the spread between feedstock and product. Cyclical but transparent.

gate2.note: Cost position, not brand: US Gulf Coast crackers on cheap shale ethane sat at the low end of the global cost curve. Record 2015 (EBITDA ~$7.5B, 2016-01-29), sustained 2016-2018. Spreads, not prices, are the asset.
Compressing: FY2019 EBITDA $5.7B (2020-01-31), ~-17% y/y, as the 2017-2019 US ethylene capacity buildout ate the ethane advantage.

gate3.note: TCEQ agreed order, $100,000, Houston Refining, from a 2014 emissions event.
Texas AG settlement $680,000 and an Illinois AG matter $125,000, both air emission events.

gate1.note: Department store: comps, gross margin, SG&A, plus owned real estate and a profit share on the Citi-issued card.

gate2.note: Positive comps FY2010-FY2014, valuable flagship real estate, Bloomingdale's differentiation. Never wide: no pricing power against off-price or online.

Comps turned negative and stayed: Q1 FY2015 -0.7% (2015-05-13), Q2 -2.1% with a guidance cut (2015-08-12), FY2016 -3.5% owned (2017-02-21). Structural (mall traffic, Amazon, off-price); the response was shrinking the store base, not raising price.

gate3.note: NY AG agreement (2014-08-20): $650,000 over racial profiling and unlawful detention of minority shoppers at Herald Square, plus a monitor and three years of compliance reporting.
Magecart card-skimming breach of macys.com.

gate1.note: Advertising/marketing services: fees and commissions, salaries the dominant cost, near-zero capital intensity. Many agencies, one economic model.

gate2.note: Scale in media buying and sticky client relationships; organic growth ~3.5-5.7% 2013-2015 and 3.5% FY2016, operating margin ~13%, very high ROIC on a near-assetless base. Not wide: accounts move on review.
Narrowing: organic growth stepped down to mid-2s (FY2018 +2.6%, FY2019 +2.8%) on client in-housing, consultancies entering, and Google/Facebook self-serve disintermediating the media role.

gate3.note: Publicis merger of equals announced 2013-07-28, terminated 2014-05-08. Strategy, not misconduct.
ANA/K2 report (2016-06-07) found cash rebates and non-transparent practices 'pervasive' in US media buying, with senior agency executives aware. Industry-level; individual agencies not named.
Two Omnicom subsidiaries subpoenaed by DOJ Antitrust (2016-12-14) in the video production bid-rigging investigation. No charges against Omnicom in the window.

gate1.note: P&C insurer with a published ten-year reserve-development table; reserving is judgment-heavy but disclosure is standard.

gate2.note: No product moat (insurance is a commodity) but durable underwriting discipline, scale and consistent favorable prior-year development. Combined ratio high-80s/low-90s in light-cat years, mid-90s in heavy ones; core ROE ~11-14%. Pricing cyclical, not proprietary.

gate3.note: Second Circuit (2014-07-22) confirmed ~$500M of previously negotiated Johns-Manville asbestos settlements were owed. A contract dispute, not misconduct.

gate1.note: Deposit-funded lender: NII on ~$1.2T of low-cost core deposits plus mortgage and fee income. Caveat: reported credit and control quality is trust-dependent, and that trust is precisely what failed.

gate2.note: Cheapest large-bank deposit base in the US, #1 mortgage originator, ROA ~1.4-1.5%, ROE ~13%. The advertised proof of the moat was the cross-sell ratio (~6.1 products/household).

The cross-sell metric was revealed on 2016-09-08 to be partly manufactured and was withdrawn; new checking account openings -44% y/y by 2016-11-17. Dated from 2017 because the revelation post-dates the 2016-06-30 anchor.
The Fed's 2018-02-02 consent order capped total assets at ~$1.95T indefinitely -- a regulator removed the growth engine, and the cap was still binding at 2020-06-30.

gate3.note: Fed cease-and-desist plus $85M penalty (2011-07-20): staff steered prime-eligible borrowers into subprime and FALSIFIED borrower income, 2004-2008, up to 10,000 borrowers. Largest Fed consumer penalty to that date. Public before EVERY WFC anchor.
DOJ fair-lending settlement (2012-07-12) $175M: Black and Hispanic borrowers steered into subprime or charged higher fees, 30,000+ borrowers, 36 states. Government finding of discrimination.
LA Times (2013-12-21): sales quotas drove employees to open unneeded accounts and forge signatures. The scandal's core facts were public here, nearly three years early.
LA City Attorney sued (May 2015) alleging quotas produced thousands of unauthorized accounts -- the fake-accounts allegation stated by a government complaint ~16 months before the CFPB order.
$1.2B FHA settlement (2016-04-08): WFC ADMITTED falsely certifying loans as FHA-eligible 2001-2008. Largest FHA origination recovery ever. Public before the 2016-06-30 anchor.
2016-09-08 CFPB/OCC/LA City Attorney $185M: ~1.5M unauthorized deposit accounts, ~623,000 unauthorized card applications; 5,300 employees already terminated. AFTER the 2016 anchor.
~570,000 auto-loan customers charged for unneeded collateral protection insurance; ~20,000 may have had vehicles repossessed.
Fed consent order citing widespread consumer abuses; asset cap imposed, board members replaced.
$1B combined CFPB/OCC penalty over auto CPI and mortgage rate-lock practices.
2020-02-21 $3B DOJ/SEC resolution with a deferred prosecution agreement; WFC admitted criminal conduct -- falsifying bank records and identity theft -- spanning 2002-2016.
